Tanya Kant was very dismissive and bias as (bad form by me, I know) I started the appointment expressing my dissatisfaction with how the NHS had failed me for years regarding severe, debilitating headaches that were put down as "migraines".

I clearly told her I had an issue with neck, jaw, kissing or looking up.
She made me bend down to touch my toes instead - Then immediately said it was all just a muscular issue.

This is after I also explained to her that I had a diagnosed shallow disc herniation that a specialist did say might be the reason for my symptoms.
I also explained to her that I was incorrectly diagnosed (classic NHS) with TMD - as I found out privately (again) that my upper jaw is not aligned.

And yet, she quite blankly with no empathy said that she still thinks its all just a muscle issue? BIAS - she had her mind set from the beginning because I had complained.

Misaligned jaw, disc herniation, had to click something back - but "just muscular issue".

Headaches that DRAMATICALLY went away after manipulating my neck - risk of hurting myself.

Of course it is "just" muscular if that is what you actively LOOK for and don't assess and examine the patient!

An Orthopedic Surgeon told me to speak to a neurologist due to more activation on my right side.

GP knows better than a specialist? okay..

No Dr has even looked or touched my neck in 3 appointments here and I can prove it.

I said my issue was looking up. Not bending down.

She lied to me by saying that she couldn't refer me back to Maxillo without the dentist note.
Except my previous practice was able to do so?

SHE EVEN HAD THE AUDACITY TO RUDELY ASK ME 'HOW THE DENTIST KNEW IT WAS NOT ALIGNED?

She just did not believe me.

Having numbness following shifting and clicking in your spine, and the same with the jaw, is not normal.
She sarcastically asked me if I had complained about my phone neurology appointment where the specialist was using loudspeaker to use AI and we couldn't hear each other properly.

I didn't know patients needed to be quizzed on if what they are saying is true.
I had to explain which test and which equipment the dentist used to confirm the jaw misalignment.
Is that normal? BIAS.
It should be the other way around.
I am the one that should have distrust of doctors after what they've made me live through for YEARS.

God forbid being frustrated at living a lie in incredible, frequent, and debilitating pain for YEARS due to negligence.

I self manipulated my neck and risked truly hurting myself, being disabled or worse.
Let that sink in, how desperate I must have been.
Headaches improved ever since clicking something back in place.
Osteopath confirmed my suspicion but that I obviously hadn't done it correctly and I might have loosened my ligaments.

"Drs" here were not apologetic like the 2 GPs who visited me at A&E and told me to get my whole spine looked at after telling them my story - following the finally diagnosed (privately) shallow disc herniation. They were shocked.

Andrew-Crawford seemed nice and apologised when I told him my full story, but he also lied to me.
He said they'd refer me to MSK. No referral was ever made.
The administration team also lied to me as I rang them twice and they said there was - but there never was one.

Afsana Safa also said that it's not normal for someone to have "all these symptoms". (not in a rude way though)

Except all these symptoms go hand in hand and actually can be completely normal if chronic and untreated?

What is not normal is for doctors to have been negligent and unprofessional whilst under their care.
